issues.description: The template StockIngredient class defines a getter named retrieveQuantity(), but other classes (Stock.java and the Main comments) expect getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs to add getters for private fields, implying conventional getX naming. This mismatch causes compilation errors in the template and will confuse students about the expected getter name.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template getter retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (or add a getQuantity() that delegates to retrieveQuantity()) so that Stock.java and other code compile and match the conventional getter naming expected by the problem statement. Update any references accordingly.

issues.description: The template's StockIngredient class exposes the ingredient quantity via retrieveQuantity(), while the rest of the code (Stock.java, Main in the template) and the solution use getQuantity(). The problem statement also instructs students to "add getters for all the private fields," which implies standard getter names like getQuantity. This mismatch (retrieveQuantity vs getQuantity) creates confusion: students may look for getQuantity() to read quantity (as used elsewhere) but only find retrieveQuantity(), or encounter compile errors in the template where getQuantity() is invoked. The solution uses getQuantity(), so the template's retrieveQuantity name appears to be an unintended inconsistency.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method retrieveQuantity() to getQuantity() (keeping the same behavior) so that getter naming is consistent with standard conventions, the problem statement expectation, and the rest of the code (Stock.java and the solution).
